newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries static in London, await FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries static in London, await FOMC.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries ticked higher in a quiet London session on Monday while players awaited the Fed's key decision on interest rates on Tuesday.
"You're not going to see anything now until the Fed make their decision. Everyone is positioned exactly where they want to be," said Nick Benton, trader at BankAmerica in London.
At 1050 GMT, the 30-year T-bond was at 96-19 to yield 6.89 percent, from 96-16 in Tokyo and 96-15 in New York.
Opinion was evenly split on whether the U.S. Federal Reserve will raise its federal funds rate at the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday, keeping traders largely sidelined.

Although a chain of mild U.S. economic data recently triggered expectations that the Fed could hold off this time, some analysts still expect a pre-emptive move to keep inflation under control. "There are justifications on both sides, but on balance we are looking for a hike," said Sonja Gibbs, bond strategist at Nomura International in London.

A rate hike of 25 basis points could lead to modest selling in Treasuries, especially on the short end of the curve. But a subsequent rise in the dollar should limit the bonds' downside, analysts said.
"Although I would expect bond yields at the long end to rise, I would expect the short rates to rise more," Gibbs said.
If, however, the Fed decided to keep its rates unchanged, Treasuries could jolt up, but not much, as upside prospects were also likely to be capped, analysts said.

One reason is most players still expect a credit tightening at the next FOMC meeting in July. Sales in the dollar, and expectations of a rate hike in Japan leading to more unwinding of yen carry trades, could also hurt Treasuries, analysts said.
By 1050 GMT, the June T-bond future was at 110-02 in automated trade, down 3/32 from Chicago's close on Friday. --Clelia Oziel, International Bonds Unit +44-171-542 8663
